3 TUI input latency in v1.17.8 (even with plugins disabled) #32859 Reports 5–10 second delays per keystroke on macOS (M1 Pro). Reproduced across iTerm2, Ghostty, and WezTerm with a clean config. 3 comments so far, rapidly gaining attention. Likely to become a top issue if not prioritized.
4 @ file mentions don't include files created after startup #32747 The file mention index is computed at startup and never refreshed. Files created mid-session are invisible to @ picker. 2 comments, 👍1. Directly impacts developer workflow — requires a restart to pick up new files.
5 Opencode hangs at startup if .git repo and inotify instances are exhausted #16610 Hard hang at startup on Linux when fs.inotify.max_user_instances is too low. A single system config change can brick the TUI experience. 11 comments, 👍7. PR #32854 (merged) now addresses this by making watcher failures non-fatal.
6 TUI "Modified Files" section completely hidden in v1.16.0 #30877 Introduced by a path truncation fix in v1.16.0, the sidebar section vanishes entirely. Developers lose visibility into uncommitted changes. 5 comments, 👍8. Affects daily workflow — should be a high priority for a patch release.
7 Immediate auto-compaction loop, model stops responding #30680 Even in a fresh empty project, OpenCode enters a runaway compaction cycle that burns tokens and then stops generating output. 7 comments, 👍0. Critical reliability bug — renders the tool unusable for affected users.
8 ACP Agent in Zed doesn't show bash commands #29924 When OpenCode is used as an ACP agent in Zed editor, bash tool calls render as invisible/empty blocks in the UI. 3 comments, 👍0. Impacts Zed + OpenCode integration — a key pairing for many developers.
9 MCP object params serialized as strings instead of objects #28472 MCP tools with type: "object" parameters receive JSON strings instead of parsed objects, causing validation failures. 4 comments, 👍1. Breaks interop with a class of MCP servers; undermines the MCP story.
10 DeepSeek API over-billing via token waste bug in v1.17.x #32911 A code bug specific to DeepSeek API integration in newer versions inflates token usage and costs for users. Corroborated on Reddit. 2 comments so far. Financially impactful — could erode trust if not addressed quickly.

4. Key PR Progress

# PR What It Does Status
1 feat: add native /goal foundation #32924 Introduces a workspace-local goal state machine with persistence and event hooks. First step toward autonomous goal pursuit in Opencode sessions. OPEN (draft)
2 feat(session): native per-session goals with /goal and autonomous pursuit #32743 Alternative/fuller implementation of per-session goals — persisted goal state with status (active/paused/completed) and autonomous agent pursuit behavior. Closes #27167 and #29445. OPEN
3 fix(core): tolerate file watcher startup failures #32854 Makes file watcher initialization non-fatal. If watcher setup fails (e.g., out of inotify instances), OpenCode logs a warning instead of hanging. Closes #16610. MERGED ✅
4 fix: /unshare does not remove share link from TUI display #32922 Fixes stale share link persisting in UI after /unshare by syncing share state immediately and cleaning up stderr output in TUI. Needs compliance review. OPEN
5 fix: MCP onprogress propagation so long-running tools don't time out #28246 Passes the onprogress callback from callTool so the MCP SDK correctly sets progressToken, preventing timeout on long-running MCP tools. Closes #28186. MERGED ✅
6 feat(plugin): add experimental.message.store.before hook #28224 New plugin hook fired inside updatePart() before a message part is written to SQLite. Enables plugins to intercept, modify, or annotate message parts. MERGED ✅
7 fix: preserve composer draft through permission prompts #28227 SolidJS <Show> unmounts PromptInput during permission prompts, destroying any typed text. This draft rework preserves the composer state across prompt/permission toggling. MERGED ✅
8 feat: expose OPENCODE_SESSION_ID env var to child processes #28185 Makes the session ID available in the environment of any child process spawned by Opencode. Currently requires DB introspection to find it — this removes that pain. MERGED ✅
9 fix: normalize forward slashes to backslashes for Windows directory matching #28251 Fixes Windows path mismatch where the web UI normalizes to forward slashes but the backend expects backslashes. MERGED ✅
10 docs: add GMI Cloud provider entry to providers directory #32914 Adds documentation and setup instructions for connecting GMI Cloud as a model provider. OPEN

5. Feature Request Trends

From the open issues, the most-requested feature directions are:

Trend Signal
Per-session goals / autonomous agent pursuit Two competing PRs (#32743, #32924) and multiple linked issues (#27167, #29445) show strong demand for goal-setting and autonomous execution beyond a single turn. This is the most active new feature direction.
Multiple auth profiles per provider #5391 — 👍31. Developers need to switch between API keys/orgs/providers without reconfiguring. Highly requested, previously filed under sst/opencode and reopened.
Automatic model selection by task type #8456 — 👍37 (highest-upvoted feature request in the dataset). Users want Opencode to route simple tasks to cheaper models and complex tasks to stronger ones.
reasoning_effort parameter support in UI #450 — 👍26, re-closed and recently updated. Multiple model families support it, but Opencode has no UI affordance.
Progress indicators for MCP calls #26328. Users have no visibility into long-running MCP tool execution.
Recursive skill discovery + multi-skill selection #21495. Current skills command is shallow; users want nested discovery and the ability to compose multiple skills.

6. Developer Pain Points

Pain Point Evidence
TUI regressions across versions Multiple recurring issues: Alpine/musl incompatibility (#27589), "Modified Files" sidebar vanishing (#30877), input latency spike (#32859), stale file indexing (#32747). The TUI is experiencing a rough patch with version-to-version stability.
File staleness / stale state File @ mentions (#32747), stale project paths after moving directories (#30697, #31888), and file index not refreshing in Desktop (#32915) all point to a systemic problem with Opencode's file watching and index invalidation.
Plugin extensibility regression The provider.models() hook breakage (#25630) means plugin authors can no longer inject custom provider models — a significant regression in the extensibility story, and one that's been open for over a month.
Windows-specific friction Path normalization bugs (#28251, #28242), stale project paths (#31888), broken self-update leaving 16-bit remnants (#28072). Windows users face a disproportionate share of paper-cut bugs.
MCP integration quality Object parameter serialization bug (#28472), missing onprogress causing tool timeouts (#28186), and general lack of progress visibility (#26328). The MCP story needs hardening before it's production-reliable.
Cost / billing confusion DeepSeek over-billing bug (#32911), mysterious FreeUsageLimitError for paid users (#32827), cancelled Zen subscription still billing (#32840), and opaque Go pricing markup (#32116). Trust in billing and cost transparency is eroding.
ACP / editor integration gaps Zed ACP agent showing empty command blocks (#29924) undermines one of Opencode's key distribution channels.

The OpenCode community is shipping fast but accumulating UI/regression debt. Priorities to watch: the /goal feature landing, TUI latency fix, and file index freshness.

Pi — badlogic/pi-mono

Pi Community Digest — 2026-06-19

1. Today's Highlights

Pi shipped v0.79.7 with automatic theme mode support, letting users configure separate light/dark themes that follow the terminal's color scheme. The community simultaneously closed a significant batch of long-running issues around TUI rendering, tool execution edge cases, and provider compatibility — a major housekeeping milestone. Active development continues on multi-session support, prompt caching for Mistral, and streaming code fence rendering.

2. Releases

v0.79.7

  • Automatic theme mode — /settings now supports separate light and dark theme selection with live terminal color-scheme detection. Requires a terminal that emits dark/light mode events. Docs →
  • Self-only updates — (details truncated in source)

3. Hot Issues

# Issue Status Why It Matters
#5700 Support multiple live agent sessions with TUI switching 🔴 OPEN Users want concurrent background agents (e.g., one refactoring while another answers questions). Currently switchSession tears down the active session. 6 comments.
#5463 Auto-compaction after final turn throws error 🔴 OPEN agent.continue() crashes when the last message is already from the assistant. 5 👍 — a real blocker for automated workflows.
#1278 @ file autocomplete should be async/streaming ✅ CLOSED Large repos caused UI freezes while fd ran synchronously. 14 comments, 16 👍 — one of the most-requested TUI fixes.
#2327 Parallel edit tool calls on the same file overwrite each other ✅ CLOSED Concurrent edits to the same file silently dropped one change. 7 comments.
#2055 Oversized image in tool result causes infinite error loop ✅ CLOSED Images exceeding Anthropic's 5MB base64 limit caused every subsequent API call to fail. 4 comments.
#2567 Compaction not working with gpt-5-mini on GitHub Copilot ✅ CLOSED gpt-5-mini rejects 'none' as a reasoning effort value — compaction needs to use 'minimal' instead. 2 comments.
#2576 Print/JSON mode doesn't emit session_shutdown ✅ CLOSED Extensions holding long-lived resources could never clean up, keeping the process alive after output completed. 3 comments.
#2557 Conflicting edits still fire tool_call event ✅ CLOSED Extensions received stale oldText for edit conflicts with no way to detect the conflict beforehand. 2 comments.
#2569 BashExecutionComponent crashes in split terminals ✅ CLOSED Ghostty split panes triggered Rendered line exceeds terminal width errors. 2 comments.
#2595 Custom renderCall/renderResult ignored for built-in tools since v0.62.0 ✅ CLOSED The v0.62.0 tool-execution rewrite silently overrode custom renderers, breaking the minimal-mode example extension. 2 comments.

4. Key PR Progress

# PR What It Does
#5874 feat(coding-agent): add automatic theme mode Implements light/dark theme selection with terminal color-scheme detection. Landed in v0.79.7.
#5884 fix(ai): handle orphaned tool result messages to prevent Moonshot 400 errors Guards against orphaned tool role messages that strict OpenAI-compatible providers reject.
#5866 feat(ai): add OpenRouter Fusion alias Adds openrouter/fusion as a synthetic router alias, matching the existing openrouter/auto pattern.
#5841 feat(tui): detect Warp terminal and enable Kitty image protocol Auto-detects Warp terminal via env vars and enables Kitty graphics + OSC 8 hyperlinks.
#5812 fix(tui): protect pipe characters inside inline code in markdown tables Fixes table rendering where backtick-wrapped `
#5796 chore: bump TS target and lib to ES2024, use Promise.withResolvers() Modernizes the TypeScript target, replacing hand-rolled Promise.withResolvers() polyfills.
#5756 feat(coding-agent): expose edit-diff for extensions Gives extensions access to diff data from edit tool calls.
#5846 fix(tui): stabilize streaming code fence rendering 🔴 OPEN — fixes glitchy rendering of code blocks during streaming output.
#5371 fix(coding-agent): add a space between skill and user messages Fixes /skill:name text rendering where the skill output and user message ran together.
#5562 fix(tui): separate list items with blank lines in loose lists Corrects CommonMark-compliant loose list rendering.

5. Feature Request Trends

  1. Multi-session / concurrent agents — Issue #5700 is the clearest signal: users want to run multiple agent sessions simultaneously and switch between them in the TUI without tearing down state.

  2. Streaming & async UX — From async @ file autocomplete (#1278) to streaming code fence rendering (#5846), the community consistently pushes for non-blocking, incremental UI updates.

  3. Extension API surface area — Multiple requests to expose internal types (ToolCallEventResult, contextUsage, edit-diff data) and fix extension hook ordering (#2543, #2557) indicate a growing ecosystem of power-users building on Pi's extension system.

  4. Provider coverage — New model providers (Mistral prompt caching #5854, Fireworks GLM #5873, OpenRouter Fusion #5866) and better thinking/reasoning toggle support (#2022, #2490) remain active areas.

  5. Terminal compatibility — Warp detection (#5841), JetBrains capabilities (#5037), Termux fixes (#2467), and WSL clipboard (#2469) show demand for broad terminal support.

6. Developer Pain Points

  • TUI freezes on large repos — Synchronous operations (file autocomplete, truncateToWidth on large strings #2447) block the main thread, degrading the experience for power users.
  • Extension system rough edges — Custom renderers silently ignored since v0.62.0 (#2595), missing type exports (#2458), and hook ordering bugs (#2543) create a frustrating experience for extension authors.
  • Thinking/reasoning toggle inconsistency — Multiple providers (Google #2490, Qwen via Anthropic compat #2022) fail to properly disable reasoning, suggesting the flag isn't plumbed consistently across provider implementations.
  • JSON mode leaking non-protocol output — Package manager progress and install notices pollute stdout in --mode json (#2482), breaking subprocess integrations.
  • Auth token caching — Shell command API keys (e.g., Azure AD tokens) are fetched once and never refreshed, causing silent failures in long-running sessions (#1835).
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-06-19

1. Today's Highlights

An active maintenance day: the v0.18.3-nightly landed with core sed-edit tracking fixes, and the contributor tt-a1i alone filed or drove fixes across token storage, OAuth, session-management, and CLI-parser bugs. Two security-adjacent bugs surfaced — workspace trust bypass for extensions/MCP and terminal OSC-code injection — both of which already have open PRs staged. On the UX front, IME cursor positioning was silently reverted in a prior PR and has now been restored.

2. Releases

v0.18.3-nightly.20260618 (bc3e0b405)

  • chore(release): v0.18.3 — release bot automated cut.
  • fix(core): Track supported sed edits in file history — ensures reversibility of sed-based file mutations in the undo stack. (PR #5255)

No stable tagged release today; changes are shipping through the nightly channel.

3. Hot Issues

# Issue Significance
#5368 MCP & extension commands ignore untrusted workspace state 🔒 A trust-bypass bug: isWorkspaceTrusted() returns an object, so !! coerces both trusted and untrusted results to true. Any workspace is treated as trusted for extension/MCP commands. Fix PR #5369 already open.
#5147 OOM on /quit with managed auto-memory + large text history After /quit, V8 hits heap limit during buildTranscriptMessages() even with zero tool calls. Affects users with long sessions. Fix PR #5181 merged.
#5370 Grep drops matches from file paths containing colons The grep parser splits on the first two colons, so paths like dir:name/file.txt are silently misparsed and matches are dropped. Open, no fix yet.
#5261 No way to expand collapsible thinking block The v0.18.2 collapsible-thinking feature shows "Thought for 1s" with no keyboard shortcut to expand. Users lost visibility into model reasoning. Closed — fix expected in next release.
#4987 PR #4779 silently reverted IME cursor positioning (PR #4652) A merged feature was accidentally rolled back inside an unrelated PR without explanation. Fix PR #4993 merged — positioning restored.
#5281 TUI becomes unresponsive due to systemd-inhibit password prompt (Linux) On headless Linux, systemd-inhibit triggers a D-Bus auth prompt that hijacks the TUI input stream. The sleep-prevention feature introduced in PR #4434 caused this. Fix PR #5318 open — passes --no-ask-password.
#5244 Windows desktop: phantom (session) entries after skill/tool use Native sessions with no real content appear as (session) in the session list. Fix PR #5245 open — filters empty sessions + fixes Windows tilde expansion.
#5363 File search cache reuses prefix results for glob patterns ResultCache incorrectly serves cached *.js results when a user later searches foo*.js, because the new query starts with a character in the old key. Fix PR #5364 open.
#5208 Stale .qwen-session marker blocks worktree cleanup across sessions A new session in a worktree created by a previous session is refused cleanup. Closed — fix shipped in recent session-management refactor.
#5343 WWW-Authenticate parser misses resource_metadata with whitespace OAuth discovery fails when the server returns resource_metadata = "..." (with spaces around =). Closed — fixed alongside other parser robustness work.

4. Key PR Progress

# PR Status Description
#5369 Pass actual TrustResult.isTrusted to ExtensionManager 🟡 Open Fixes the coerced-boolean trust bypass [#5368]. Adds regression tests for explicit untrusted workspaces. High-priority security fix.
#5318 Pass --no-ask-password to systemd-inhibit 🟡 Open Resolves TUI freeze on Linux headless SSH sessions [#5281]. Prevents D-Bus auth prompt from hijacking stdin in the TUI.
#5362 Honor tools.useBuiltinRipgrep setting at runtime 🟡 Open The configured ripgrep preference was not actually propagated to the execution path. Adds bundled-vs-system resolution caching.
#5364 Avoid glob prefix cache reuse in file search 🟡 Open Fixes [#5363]. Uses picomatch's glob scanner to invalidate stale cache entries for pattern queries.
#5221 Fall back to encrypted-file storage for extension secrets 🟢 Closed When the OS keychain is unavailable (e.g., headless Linux, CI), secrets now use AES-256-GCM encrypted files instead of failing outright.
#4993 Restore IME physical cursor positioning 🟢 Closed Reverts the accidental rollback of PR #4652 inside PR #4779. Fixes [#4987].
#5181 Prevent OOM during auto-memory transcript build on /quit 🟢 Closed Fixes [#5147] by reducing buildTranscriptMessages() memory pressure — avoids structuredClone and full-history copy on quit.
#4850 Interactive multi-tab /extensions manager 🟡 Open Transforms /extensions from a flat read-only list into a tabbed UI (Installed / Discover / Sources). Covers full extension lifecycle.
#5319 Rename TodoWrite display name → "TodoList" 🟢 Closed User-facing rename across TUI, web-shell, and webui. Wire name todo_write unchanged — no tool-call breakage.
#3975 Add /directory remove subcommand 🟡 Open Long-requested pairing for /directory add. Allows removing directories from workspace context with scope-aware settings cleanup.

5. Feature Request Trends

Token & usage telemetry — Issue #4479 reflects strong demand for daily token-consumption dashboards. Users report 30 M-token sessions with no built-in visibility.

Channel ecosystem expansion — The QQ Bot adapter request #5202 underscores demand for deeper integration into regional platforms (WeChat, DingTalk, Feishu, now QQ).

Estimated response time — Feature request #5366 asks for a toggle to show/hide the model's estimated completion time — a UX polish item with moderate community interest.

Session management polish — Multiple requests (#5244, #5208) for worktree cleanup, phantom-session filtering, and cross-session state hygiene signal that the sessions workflow is a current friction surface.

6. Developer Pain Points

Parser correctness is a recurring theme. Today's issues reveal a pattern of incomplete parseInt() / string-split / regex-based parsers that accept malformed input: cron fields (#5348), ACP timeouts (#5313), OpenAI schema constraints (#5310), MCP prompt args (#5322), sandbox image names (#5324), and OSC terminal sequences (#5304). A common root cause: validation uses lenient JS coercion instead of strict token-level parsing.

OAuth & token-storage robustness. At least 5 issues/PRs today (#5355, #5359, #5365, #5367) trace to edge cases in token expiry calculation, first-save file creation, and expires_in=0 handling across BaseTokenStorage and MCP OAuth paths.

Platform-specific edge cases on Windows (tilde path expansion, phantom sessions) and Linux (systemd-inhibit blocking TUI) continue to surface, indicating that cross-platform desktop testing coverage needs reinforcement.

Trust model correctness. The workspace-trust coercion bug #5368 is a systemic type-safety issue — a TrustResult object passed through !! silently breaks the entire trust boundary for extensions and MCP servers.

Data source: github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code — refreshed 2026-06-19.

DeepSeek TUI — Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI

CodeWhale TUI Community Digest — 2026-06-19

1. Today's Highlights

The project has officially rebranded from deepseek-tui to CodeWhale (v0.8.62); the legacy npm package is deprecated and users should follow docs/REBRAND.md to migrate. Today's activity is dominated by a wave of reliability fixes — session persistence after stalls, delegated server child cleanup, and Kimi/Moonshot parameter sanitization — alongside a major internal refactoring push targeting Rust monoliths across the TUI crate. The community continues to report TUI freezes and agent scope-discipline failures as the most urgent pain points.

2. Releases

  • v0.8.62 — Rebrand release. The canonical project, command, npm package, and release-asset name is now CodeWhale. The legacy deepseek-tui npm package is deprecated with no further releases. Migration guide: docs/REBRAND.md. → github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/releases

3. Hot Issues

# Issue Why It Matters Community Signal
#2487 Turn stalled — no completion signal received The most-commented issue (16 comments). In yolo mode the TUI freezes and becomes unresponsive; even continue cannot resume. Affects core reliability for power users. 👍1, active discussion through June 18
#1812 TUI freeze on Windows (crossterm poll) Intermittent total UI lockup on Windows 11 — no keyboard input, no screen updates, process stays alive. Two confirmed events with logs and thread-state analysis. Cross-platform reliability is a key adoption barrier. 7 comments, detailed repro
#3275 Agent over-extends scope, self-questions and self-answers Regression from #3061. The agent enters a self-driven loop of proposing, answering, and executing without user confirmation — a serious trust and safety concern for production use. 5 comments, labeled security + reliability
#3289 UI freeze after auto-spawning multiple sub-agents In plan mode, after the agent auto-spawns several sub-agents, the UI freezes. Directly impacts the multi-agent workflow that CodeWhale is building toward. 4 comments, reproducible steps
#3238 Fails on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS due to glibc mismatch Blocks an entire Linux user segment. The npm install succeeds but the binary won't run. This is now partially addressed by the musl static build PR (#3274). 3 comments
#3240 Legacy .deepseek config directory still created at runtime Post-rebrand, the tool still creates ~/.deepseek alongside ~/.codewhale on Windows. Confusing for users who expect a clean migration. 3 comments
#3315 Enforce real user-input provenance for write/continue approvals Follow-up to #3275: the agent allegedly generated its own approval-like text (e.g., 改吧) and treated it as authorization. This is a prompt-injection-adjacent security issue. 1 comment, opened June 18 by maintainer
#3304 Expose editable sub-agent recursion and concurrency controls Sub-agent runtime limits exist in config but aren't editable from the TUI. Users want first-class controls for recursion depth and launch limits. 2 comments, maintainer-opened
#2973 Replace MockWorkflowExecutor with production async executor Core WhaleFlow infrastructure still uses a mock executor. The real executor needs bounded concurrency, cancellation, cost budgets, and control-flow nodes. 2 comments, maintainer-owned
#2608 Extract provider registry from ballooning config files config.rs is 4,719 lines; tui/src/config.rs is 9,402 lines. Every new provider requires touching 15–30 match arms. This is the root cause of much of the codebase's scaling pain. 2 comments, maintainer-owned

4. Key PR Progress

# PR Description Status
#3285 Persist session before stall/cancel recovery Fixes #2739 (partial). Ensures the session is saved before the stall watchdog or cancel path clears turn bookkeeping, so --continue preserves history. ✅ Merged
#3286 Ensure type:object on Kimi parameters root for all schema shapes Fixes #3281. The previous sanitization only handled narrow conditions; now $ref, allOf, anyOf, oneOf root schemas are also covered, preventing 400 errors from Moonshot. ✅ Merged
#3283 Fix Plan/Agent mode toggle — approval_mode restore + auto-execution guard Fixes #3279. approval_mode is now correctly restored after Plan→Agent switch, and an auto-execution guard prevents the agent from running plans without explicit user confirmation. ✅ Merged
#3290 Add scope_discipline rules to prevent self-questioning agent loops Adds 47 lines to constitution.md with explicit rules preventing the agent from entering self-sustaining question/answer cycles. Addresses #3275 at the prompt level. ✅ Merged
#3295 Wire ask permission rules into TUI runtime approval path Loads permissions.toml ask-rules into the ExecPolicyEngine and applies them at runtime for exec_shell tool calls. Complements PR #3301. ✅ Merged
#3301 Save ask permission rules from approvals UI Adds an s shortcut in the approval modal to persist the current shell approval as a permissions.toml ask rule with a TOML preview. 🔄 Open
#3300 Preserve thinking/tool blocks when seeding thread from session Replaces text-only seed_thread_from_messages with a block-type-aware implementation so Thinking, ToolUse, and ToolResult blocks survive session reconstruction. 🔄 Open
#3277 Workrooms Phase 1 — data model, endpoints, docs Foundation layer for the v0.9.0 Workroom abstraction: a chat-native, durable container for threaded agent conversations. Includes a 242-line RFC. ✅ Merged
#3274 Build static Linux x64 binaries with musl Switches Linux release builds from dynamic glibc to static musl, resolving the Ubuntu 22.04 glibc mismatch issue (#3238) for release artifacts. ✅ Merged
#3317 Tear down delegated serve/app-server child on dispatcher exit Fixes #3259 (partial). Ensures the delegated codewhale-tui listener is terminated when the dispatcher is killed, preventing orphaned processes. 🔄 Open

5. Feature Request Trends

  1. Sub-agent orchestration controls — Users want editable recursion depth, concurrency limits, and better visibility into sub-agent lifecycle from the TUI (#3304, #3289, #2973). The WhaleFlow swarm synthesis pass (#3230) is the next architectural milestone.

  2. Permission system maturation — A cluster of issues and PRs (#3301, #3295, #3264, #3296) shows strong demand for granular, persistent permission rules scoped to ~/.codewhale/skills/ and permissions.toml, with ask-only workflows and skill-scan restrictions.

  3. Provider ecosystem expansion — Requests for OpenCode Go/Zen (#1481), Atlas Cloud (#3239), and the provider registry refactor (#2608) all point to demand for easier multi-provider support without touching 15–30 match arms per addition.

  4. Workroom abstraction — The Workrooms Phase 1 PR (#3277) and its RFC signal a shift toward chat-native, durable conversation containers as a first-class concept for v0.9.0.

  5. Approval UX improvements — Plan/Agent mode toggle consistency (#3279 → #3283), scope discipline (#3275 → #3290), and user-input provenance enforcement (#3315) all reflect demand for the agent to be more predictable and less autonomous.

6. Developer Pain Points

  • TUI freezes are the #1 reliability complaint. Three distinct freeze vectors are tracked: Windows crossterm polling (#1812), turn stalls with no completion signal (#2487), and sub-agent auto-spawn overload (#3289). The common thread is the TUI event loop becoming unresponsive while the process stays alive — users lose work and must restart.

  • Session/continuity loss after stalls. Even when the agent doesn't crash, a stalled turn followed by --continue loses the entire in-progress session (#2739). PR #3285 addresses the data-loss part, but the underlying stall detection remains fragile.

  • Agent scope discipline. Multiple users report the agent exceeding its mandate — self-questioning, self-answering, and executing without confirmation (#3275, #3279). The team is addressing this at both the prompt level (constitution rules in #3290) and the approval architecture level (#3315).

  • Post-rebrand rough edges. The rename to CodeWhale is official, but legacy .deepseek directories are still created at runtime (#3240), and documentation/tooling references are still being updated (#3316).

  • Rust codebase scaling. The maintainer has opened a systematic series of refactoring issues (#3306–#3314) targeting monoliths in config.rs (9,402 lines), app.rs (~150 fields), runtime_threads.rs (2,400-line impl), and ui.rs (large run_event_loop). This is a leading indicator that contributor onboarding and feature velocity are being impacted by codebase complexity.

Data source: github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale (formerly Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI). Digest generated by OWL for 2026-06-19.

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目动态日报 — 2026-06-19

1. 今日速览

OpenClaw 今日处于高活跃、高积压状态。过去 24 小时内 Issues 更新 500 条（新开/活跃 475 条，关闭仅 25 条），PR 更新 500 条（待合并 463 条，已合并/关闭仅 37 条），净积压持续扩大。无新版本发布。项目当前的核心矛盾集中在消息投递可靠性（Telegram/Discord/Slack 多通道丢消息）、会话状态管理（compaction 旋转、子代理交付、cron 竞争）以及认证与提供者配置三大领域。维护者审查速度明显跟不上社区贡献节奏，463 个待合并 PR 和大量标记 needs-maintainer-review 的 Issue 表明项目正面临严重的审查瓶颈。

横向生态对比

个人 AI 助手/自主智能体开源生态横向对比分析报告

报告日期：2026-06-19 | 分析项目数：14 | 生成：OWL

1. 生态全景

2026 年 6 月中旬，个人 AI 助手开源生态处于高活跃、高分化的并行发展期。OpenClaw 以 500+ Issues / 500+ PR 的日更新量成为生态绝对核心，但 463 个待合并 PR 和 5% 的 Issue 关闭率暴露出严重的审查瓶颈，折射出社区贡献热情与维护者带宽之间的结构性矛盾。第二梯队的 NanoBot、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、CoPaw、ZeroClaw 均处于密集功能迭代期，日 PR 更新在 25-50 条区间，合并节奏明显更快。安全议题正在成为全生态的共同焦点——TinyClaw、LobsterAI、ZeroClaw、NanoClaw 均在今日收到高危安全报告，涉及未认证访问、任意文件读取、SSRF 等体系性安全缺口，说明随着 Agent 从"玩具"走向"半生产"，安全审计已成为不可回避的刚需。上下文管理（compaction、consolidation、scroll 策略）和消息投递可靠性（多通道丢消息）是横跨多个项目的两大技术痛点，表明 Agent 的"长对话一致性"和"多渠道可达性"仍是行业尚未解决的基础难题。

3. OpenClaw 在生态中的定位

规模绝对领先，但效率是短板。 OpenClaw 的日 Issues 更新量（500）和 PR 更新量（500）均超过其余 13 个项目之和，GitHub 生态影响力无可争议。与同类项目相比：

维度 OpenClaw 最接近的竞争者
社区规模 500+ Issues/天，463 PR 积压 Hermes Agent（50/天）、ZeroClaw（50/天）——差一个数量级
通道覆盖 Telegram/Discord/Slack/Feishu/WhatsApp/WebChat/Android Node NanoBot（Feishu/WhatsApp）、IronClaw（Slack/WeCom）、CoPaw（钉钉/飞书/微信/QQ）
技术路线 自研 gateway + 多 provider 适配 + 动态工具系统 ZeroClaw 偏向安全隔离和 pipeline 架构；CoPaw 深度绑定 AgentScope 2.0；NanoBot 强调轻量和并发安全
核心优势 通道覆盖最广、社区贡献最活跃、功能最全面 —
核心劣势 审查瓶颈严重（5% Issue 关闭率）、消息投递可靠性差（多通道丢消息 P1 长期未解）、性能退化（CLI 冷启动 14s） —

技术路线差异： OpenClaw 走的是"大而全"的平台路线，自研 gateway 层统一多通道接入，动态工具系统支持运行时工具发现。相比之下，ZeroClaw 更强调安全隔离（credential redaction 层、per-agent tool gating、shell 内存上限），CoPaw 正在向 AgentScope 2.0 原生能力迁移，NanoBot 则聚焦并发安全和轻量化。OpenClaw 的架构复杂度远高于同类项目，这是其审查瓶颈的结构性原因。

4. 共同关注的技术方向

以下需求在多个项目中同时涌现，代表行业共性挑战：

① 上下文管理与 Compaction 可靠性

涉及项目：OpenClaw、NanoBot、Hermes Agent、CoPaw（全部 4 个第一梯队项目）

  • OpenClaw：compaction 旋转丢弃 assistant 回复（#76729）、post-turn compaction 失败导致回复丢失（#94688）
  • NanoBot：consolidation 丢失 delivery 消息（#4307）、eager consolidation 需求（#4402）
  • Hermes Agent：/compress 删除原始消息（#44794）、context compression 静默丢失未刷新消息（#47202）
  • CoPaw：子 Agent compaction 导致进程冻结（#5218）、人设文件被压缩丢失（#5171）

行业信号： 上下文压缩是 Agent 长对话能力的核心，但目前所有项目的实现都存在"压缩后信息丢失"的问题。CoPaw 正在探索 Headroom 外部可逆压缩 + scroll 检索驱动策略的分层方案，可能是行业方向。

② 消息投递可靠性（多通道丢消息）

涉及项目：OpenClaw、NanoClaw、CoPaw

  • OpenClaw：Telegram 静默丢消息（#80520）、Discord 畸形 payload（#81484）、Slack 线程无法投递（#78061）、回复不回传原始通道（#54531）
  • NanoClaw：Discord 长文截断（#2812）
  • CoPaw：飞书群聊回复路由到私聊（#5264）

行业信号： 多通道消息投递是 Agent 从"开发工具"走向"日常助手"的关键门槛。OpenClaw 的 P1 问题已标记 stale 且社区不满情绪明显，说明这是用户最痛但最难解决的问题。

③ 安全与权限隔离

涉及项目：TinyClaw、LobsterAI、ZeroClaw、NanoClaw、OpenClaw、Hermes Agent

  • TinyClaw：未认证 API 权限绕过（#284）、任意文件读取（#283）、文件外发（#282）
  • LobsterAI：自动 artifact 加载导致任意本地文件读取（#2176）
  • ZeroClaw：execute_pipeline 绕过 per-agent tool gating（#7947）、SSRF 防护（#7902）
  • NanoClaw：非 Owner 成员可创建持久子 Agent（#2807）、send_file 路径穿越（#2817）
  • OpenClaw：tools.deny 对 MCP 不生效（#79451）、exec 无法访问 private-LAN（#94032）
  • Hermes Agent：子 profile 下 state.db 为空导致会话数据丢失（#48519）

行业信号： 安全议题在 6 月 19 日集中爆发，涉及认证绕过、文件越权、SSRF、权限隔离等多个维度。随着 Agent 开始处理敏感数据和操作本地系统，安全审计已从"加分项"变为"必选项"。

④ 会话状态管理

涉及项目：OpenClaw、NanoBot、NullClaw、Moltis

7. 值得关注的趋势信号

趋势 1：Agent 安全从"可选"变为"刚需"

信号强度：🔴🔴🔴 极高

今日 TinyClaw（3 个高危）、LobsterAI（1 个高危）、ZeroClaw（S0 混淆代理漏洞）、NanoClaw（2 个安全 Issue）共收到 7 个高危安全报告，涉及认证绕过、文件越权、SSRF、权限隔离。安全研究者 YLChen-007 在 LobsterAI 和 TinyClaw 的系统性审计表明，外部安全社区已开始关注 AI Agent 生态。对开发者的建议： 在架构设计阶段就引入安全审查，而非事后修补；建立 SECURITY.md 和安全响应流程；对文件操作、API 入口、子代理权限实施最小权限原则。

趋势 2：上下文管理正在从"简单截断"走向"分层策略"

信号强度：🔴🔴🔴 极高

CoPaw 的 Headroom 外部可逆压缩（#5244）+ scroll 检索驱动策略（#5321）代表了上下文管理的最新方向——不再依赖单一的 compaction，而是形成"原生压缩 + 可插拔策略 + 检索召回"的分层体系。NanoBot 的 eager consolidation（#4402）和 OpenClaw 的 session history 跨 reset 查找（#90239）同样指向这一趋势。对开发者的建议： 上下文管理不应是单一的 trim/summarize，而应提供可配置的多策略选项（保留最近 N 条、锁定人设文件、外部压缩、检索召回）。

趋势 3：多 Agent 协作从"自由流转"走向"受控协作"

信号强度：🔴🔴🔴 高

NanoClaw 今日合并了 Agent-to-Agent 逐条审批策略（#2793），OpenClaw 的 MCP 工具调用审批（#78308）和 Hermes Agent 的 delegate_task 跨 profile 支持（#35409）都指向同一方向：多 Agent 协作需要细粒度的权限控制。对开发者的建议： 多 Agent 系统应默认提供审批机制，而非完全自由的消息流转；需要支持 per-agent 的 tool access policy 和跨 agent 的身份认证。

趋势 4：桌面端体验成为差异化竞争焦点

信号强度：🔴🔴 中高

Hermes Agent 的桌面端 zoom 控制（#40166，👍6）、LobsterAI 的 Computer Use MVP 和语音输入重构、NullClaw 的 ESP32 嵌入式探索，表明 Agent 的交互形态正在从"命令行 + Web"扩展到桌面端、移动端、嵌入式。对开发者的建议： 桌面端用户期望的是"原生应用体验"而非"Web 套壳"，需要关注字体缩放、主题、离线能力、系统集成等细节。

趋势 5：消息投递可靠性是用户留存的关键门槛

信号强度：🔴🔴🔴 极高

OpenClaw 的 P1 消息投递问题（#54531）已标记 stale 且社区不满持续积累，CoPaw 的飞书路由错误（#5264）和 NanoClaw 的 Discord 截断（#2812）表明这不是个例。对开发者的建议： 消息投递应作为核心功能而非附加功能来对待；需要端到端的投递确认机制（sendMessage 日志、投递状态回执）；多通道场景下需要严格的会话路由隔离。

趋势 6：生态正在从"单一 Agent"走向"Agent 平台"

信号强度：🔴🔴 中

IronClaw 的 Projects 系列（5 层 PR 栈）、OpenClaw 的 snapshot CLI（#94717）和 session history 跨 reset 查找（#90239）、NanoClaw 的 Agent-to-Agent 审批，都表明项目正在从"运行单个 Agent"向"管理 Agent 生态"演进。对开发者的建议： 平台化是必然趋势，需要提前考虑多 Agent 管理、项目/工作区隔离、Agent 生命周期管理（创建/重命名/删除/归档）等基础设施。

  • 链接：https://github.com/sipeed/picoclaw/issues/3094
